content: The concentration of the drug is 5 mg/mL, which has the potential to cause toxicity. The recommended dosage is 570 mcg/kg, administered orally twice daily, 30 minutes before a meal. Gastrointestinal disorders associated with the drug include hematemesis, liver transplant, post-endoscopy hemorrhage, and post-liver biopsy hemorrhage. General disorders and conditions at the administration site include drug ineffectiveness. Injuries, poisoning, and procedural complications may occur, including off-label use. Laboratory investigations have shown increased gamma-glutamyl transferase levels. Nervous system disorders such as intracranial hemorrhage have been reported. Patients with prior or active hepatic decompensation events, such as variceal hemorrhage, ascites, or hepatic encephalopathy, may experience hepatotoxicity. Maternal use of the drug at the recommended dose is not expected to result in measurable fetal exposure due to low systemic absorption following oral administration. No developmental effects were observed in animal reproduction studies. The low absorption following oral administration also suggests that breastfeeding is not expected to expose the infant to the drug at the recommended dose. However, data on the presence of the drug in human milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production are not available. Patients with Alagille syndrome (ALGS) or progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC) may have fat-soluble vitamin (FSV) deficiencies as part of their disease. Therapy with this drug may reduce the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins. Therefore, FSV levels should be monitored, and FSV intake should be supplemented if a deficiency is observed during lactation. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s need for therapy and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child from the treatment or the underlying maternal condition. The drug is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. The pharmacy provides oral dosing dispensers in 5-mL, 1-mL, or 3-mL sizes to accurately measure and deliver the prescribed dose. Refer to the prescribing information to select the appropriate dosing dispenser size. Unopened bottles should be stored at 20-25°C (68-77°F), with excursions permitted between 15-30°C (59-86°F). Opened bottles should be stored at temperatures ≤30°C (86°F), and any remaining solution should be discarded 100 days after opening.
